title: feat(editor): add getSelectedText(), multi-line list toggle, and atomic replaceRange

reviews.body:
The implementation is directionally strong: the half-open line range handling, reversed-selection tests, and atomic `replaceRange` approach are all good. I am requesting changes for repo process and source hygiene before this can merge.

1. This PR adds public core API (`getSelectedText`, `replaceRange`) and changes toolbar behavior, but it does not include an OpenSpec change. Please add `openspec/changes/...` with deltas for the core API and toolbar list-toggle semantics, then run `openspec validate <change-id> --strict`.

2. `PR_DESCRIPTION.md` should not be committed as a source file. Please move that content into the GitHub PR description and remove the file from the branch.

3. `replaceRange()` is now a public `EditorAPI` method, but the direct tests live only indirectly through toolbar behavior. Please add focused core tests for the primitive itself, especially range replacement plus selection in one dispatch and the `silent` option matching `setDocument` semantics.

I ran `pnpm vitest run packages/core/test/editor.test.ts packages/plugin-toolbar/test/plugin-toolbar.test.ts`, `pnpm --filter @floatboat/nexus-core build`, and `pnpm --filter @floatboat/nexus-plugin-toolbar build`; all passed locally.

issue_comments.body:
Thanks for the detailed review @ketd. All three items addressed in the amended commit:
**1. OpenSpec change** — Added `openspec/changes/add-selection-api/` with `proposal.md`, `tasks.md`, and spec deltasfor `editor-core` (`getSelectedText` + `replaceRange` requirements with scenarios) and `plugin-toolbar` (range-awarelist toggle semantics).
**2. `PR_DESCRIPTION.md`** — Removed from the branch (`git rm`). Content already lives in the GitHub PR description.
**3. Focused `replaceRange()` core tests** — Added 5 direct tests to `packages/core/test/editor.test.ts` covering : basic range replacement, selection repositioned in same dispatch, collapsed range insert, `silent` option suppresses`onChange` but keeps AST consistent, and exactly-one-undo-entry (using `createHistoryPlugin()` to activate CM6 history, same pattern as the toolbar atomic-undo suite). All 27 core tests pass.
